issues.description: validate_conda substring match accepts any binary whose --version output contains 'conda' or 'mamba'
issues.detail: `any(tool in out.decode().lower() ...)` matches substrings anywhere in output, so 'anaconda-project', a path like /opt/anaconda/bin/foo, or any string containing 'mamba' passes. The postcondition 'binary identifies as conda/mamba/micromamba' is not actually established. Check the first token or match a known program name instead.

issues.description: filters='*.exe' restricts browse dialog to Windows executables on macOS/Linux
issues.detail: conda, mamba, and micromamba on POSIX systems are extensionless binaries. Users on Linux/macOS opening the browse dialog will see no matching files and must defeat the filter. Either condition the filter on sys.platform or drop it; validate_conda already enforces correctness.

issues.description: validate_conda conflates 'empty/unset' with 'verified executable' in one ambiguous boolean
issues.detail: Returning True for an empty string so preferences won't flag an empty field violates the docstring postcondition ('points to a working conda-like executable'). The three orthogonal facts — empty, executable file, --version identifies as conda — are folded into one True/False. Separate the predicates or return structured information.

issues.description: argv() uses the custom conda path without re-validating it at use time
issues.detail: When auto-detect fails, the kernelspec falls back to the user-configured conda_path without re-checking that it still exists, is executable, or is conda. The preferences validator runs only on entry; nothing preserves the invariant across the config boundary. Also, custom_conda boolean and conda_path string carry redundant information — a non-empty path could suffice.

issues.description: validate_conda subprocess has no timeout and may run on every keystroke
issues.detail: run_program(...).communicate() has no timeout, so a hung or misidentified binary blocks the preferences UI thread indefinitely. Additionally, if wired to textChanged, each keystroke spawns conda --version (hundreds of ms). Add a timeout and debounce to editingFinished or focus-out.

issues.description: validate_conda mixes early returns with a trailing 'return valid', obscuring the predicate's structure
issues.detail: The function mixes early `return False`/`return True` with a final `return valid` depending on a mutated flag. A reader must simulate the control flow to verify there is no path returning the initial False after success. Restructure as guard clauses or a single boolean expression for legibility.

synthesis.summary: The patch adds a user-configurable conda path with validation, a preferences widget, and a kernelspec fallback. The panel agrees the validator is the weak point: substring matching admits false positives, the '*.exe' filter is Windows-only, empty-string is conflated with 'valid', and the subprocess has no timeout. The kernelspec consumes the custom path without re-validating it, breaking the 'valid conda executable' invariant across the config boundary. No P0 blockers — the structure is sound, but the validator's correctness argument and its lifetime guarantees need work before merge.
